The assumption that there is no air resistance is a standard simplification in introductory physics to make projectile motion calculations tractable using basic kinematic equations. While real-world projectiles experience drag, neglecting it allows for the application of uniform acceleration due to gravity, which is also assumed to be constant near the Earth's surface. These assumptions are mathematically valid within the context of idealized models, even if they do not perfectly represent reality.

The animal with distinctive black and white stripes is the zebra.
